TrendsInterestResponse.description:
Search-attention series returned by ``GET /api/trends/interest``.

Values are Google's relative index: 100 is the highest point on or before
``anchor_date``, and everything else is scaled against it. There are no
absolute search counts, and a 0 can mean "below Google's reporting
threshold" rather than "nobody searched it".

anchor_date.description: Last date that could contribute to the 0-100 scale. Equals end_date for a raw fetch, or the as_of date after rebasing.
anchor_date.title: Anchor Date

fetched_at.description: UTC fetch time in ISO format
fetched_at.title: Fetched At

granularity.description: Point spacing Google returned: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly
granularity.title: Granularity

is_partial.description: True marks a still-accumulating period, aligned with dates
is_partial.title: Is Partial

keywords.description: Keywords extracted from the query; all share one scale
keywords.title: Keywords

values.description: Keyword to its series, aligned with dates
values.title: Values

get.description:
Return search attention for the same keywords and window as a search.

Declared as a plain function rather than an async one on purpose. The
Google Trends library blocks on HTTP and also sleeps to space requests
out, so FastAPI runs this in its worker thread pool and the event loop
stays free for article searches.

parameters.description: The same keyword query used for article search. Boolean operators and excluded terms are removed, quoted phrases are kept whole, and at most 5 keywords are used.
parameters.name: q

schema.description: The same keyword query used for article search. Boolean operators and excluded terms are removed, quoted phrases are kept whole, and at most 5 keywords are used.
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: Inclusive window start (YYYY-MM-DD)
parameters.name: start

schema.description: Inclusive window start (YYYY-MM-DD)
schema.title: Start

parameters.description: Inclusive window end (YYYY-MM-DD)
parameters.name: end

schema.description: Inclusive window end (YYYY-MM-DD)
schema.title: End

parameters.description: Geography code such as US or US-NY. Empty uses the configured default, which is worldwide unless changed.
parameters.name: geo

schema.description: Geography code such as US or US-NY. Empty uses the configured default, which is worldwide unless changed.
schema.title: Geo

parameters.description: Optional decision date (YYYY-MM-DD) inside the window. When given, later points are dropped and the series is rescaled to the highest value up to that date, removing the future peak that Google's own scaling would otherwise encode.
parameters.name: as_of

schema.description: Optional decision date (YYYY-MM-DD) inside the window. When given, later points are dropped and the series is rescaled to the highest value up to that date, removing the future peak that Google's own scaling would otherwise encode.
schema.title: As Of
